text.autoconfig.spatialhud.title: Spatial HUD
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideO: The purple horizontal panel is a flat purple panel in the world, client side only. It shows your lower HUD inside its border: the hotbar, status bars, experience, held item name and the slot cycling display. Presets: choose where it sits. Waist keeps it at your feet and body heading. Face keeps it fixed in your view, square to you. Two custom presets are yours to set. Panel: its width, heading, border, fill, occlusion and shoulder camera. Wiggle: how it lags behind your turns and movement. HUD Contents: which parts of the HUD appear, and the picture offset.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideP: Waist and Face are the two starting placements. Waist lies flat at your feet, so look down to see it. Face stays square to your view at a set distance and height. The wiggle still lags it behind your turns and movement. Set distances and heights in the Presets tab, and width, border and occlusion in the Panel tab.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.enable: Master switch for Spatial HUD. Turning this off in Setup immediately restores the normal vanilla HUD and hides the purple test surface. The separately bindable Toggle Spatial HUD control changes this exact same saved switch.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showPa: Method 3 only. Draws the subtle translucent backing behind the selected lower-HUD surface, in the same private texture as the icons and text, so it receives the same world-space deformation. Method 4 has no backing: its purple fill is controlled by Show Purple Fill.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.onlyDu: Keep the spatial presentation out of inventories, chat, pause menus, Mod Menu, and other screens. This is recommended for normal play. Turn it off to show the panel and HUD over those screens as well.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.render: Move this slider to choose the active panel: 3 is the real 3D world-space flat map, 4 is the purple horizontal panel anchored to your feet.
Legacy saved value. Use Render Mode Slider above instead.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.distan: Shared placement distance in block-like units, measured forward from the player-local panel origin. Method 3 is placed by the anchor below. Increasing this makes the panel appear farther away and smaller in perspective; extremely low values are clamped to keep the plane in front of the camera.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.horizo: Panel Width (blocks)
Width of the purple panel while the Waist preset is active, in blocks. The height follows the HUD's proportions. Wider shows more of the hotbar and slot cycling.
Panel Width (blocks)
Width of the purple panel while the Face preset is active, in blocks. The height follows the HUD's proportions. Wider shows more of the hotbar and slot cycling.
Panel Width (blocks)
Width of the purple panel while the Custom 1 preset is active, in blocks. The height follows the HUD's proportions. Wider shows more of the hotbar and slot cycling.
Panel Width (blocks)
Width of the purple panel while the Custom 2 preset is active, in blocks. The height follows the HUD's proportions. Wider shows more of the hotbar and slot cycling.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeW: Width of the purple panel, in blocks. The height follows the HUD's proportions. Wider shows more of the hotbar and slot cycling.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Move the panel sideways within its active horizontal anchor. Positive values move right and negative values move left. With Method 3 set to Camera Yaw, right and left follow the view; with Player Body, they follow the body heading instead.

Move the whole panel up or down relative to eye height. Negative values place it at waist height, as if a flat Minecraft map rests in front of you; positive values raise it. This changes position only—use the three rotation controls below to change the surface itself.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.minimu: This old JSON field is no longer used. Spatial HUD now culls only from real physical depth and viewport intersection, never from a configured camera-pitch cutoff.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Primary Flat-Map Tilt — Left ↔ Right Axis

Rotate the surface around its own left-to-right axis. The 85 degree default is almost horizontal, like a Minecraft map laid flat and viewed from above. Lower values create a deliberately steeper paper-like angle. This is a physical surface angle, not a camera-follow setting.
Fine Tilt Offset — Left ↔ Right Axis

Small additional rotation around the same left-to-right axis as Primary Flat-Map Tilt. Positive values push the far/top edge farther away; negative values pull it closer. Leave this at 0 unless fine-tuning the primary tilt, so the two controls do not unintentionally cancel each other.

Rotate the complete flat map around the player-local vertical up axis. Positive values turn its right edge farther forward and its left edge closer; negative values do the opposite. This is not camera yaw: it deliberately angles the surface left or right within the active horizontal anchor.

Rotate around the axis perpendicular to the paper surface. Positive values raise the right edge and lower the left edge; negative values reverse that slope. It is provided for deliberate three-axis adjustment, but 0 keeps text level and is the recommended normal-play value.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.worldS: Applies only to Method 3. Camera Yaw keeps the physical plane in front while looking left or right, as the other panel placements do. Player Body keeps it at body heading instead, so it can remain at the side while the camera looks elsewhere.

Applies only to Method 3. When enabled, the HUD texture uses the world depth buffer, so terrain or a block between the camera and the plane hides it like a physical object. Disable it to retain the world-space position but draw the panel visibly through terrain.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHo: Include the hotbar plus the vanilla spectator menu and spectator tooltip in the spatial panel. Disable this if another HUD mod owns the hotbar or if you want Spatial HUD to present only the status information around it.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showBa: Include the main vanilla status-bar roots: armor, health, hunger, and air. The enlarged lower-HUD source surface carries these roots alongside the hotbar, experience, and held-item information. Decorations injected into selected roots are captured with them.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showXp: Include the vanilla experience progress bar, level number, and adjacent information-bar root. Disable it when another mod supplies a replacement experience display or when a cleaner hotbar-only panel is preferred.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showMo: Include the vanilla mount-health root while riding an entity. It has no effect while no mount-health HUD is active.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHe: Include the transient selected-item name above the lower HUD panel. Disable it if a tooltip or inventory mod already provides a preferred held-item label.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.horizo: Waist: Distance
Waist preset only. How far in front of your feet the centre of the purple panel sits, in blocks. Larger values move it further away from you.
Waist: Height Above Feet
Waist preset only. Height of the purple panel above your feet, in blocks. Your eyes are about 1.6 blocks up, so values near 0.9 put it at about waist height.
Panel Curve (degrees)
Bends the purple panel around you, like a curved gaming monitor. 0 is flat. Up to 120 degrees. The panel keeps its width along the curve. Applies to all presets.
Feet Panel Angle

The look-down angle at which the purple panel faces you square-on. 90 lies it flat, so it faces the sky. Smaller angles tilt its near edge toward you. Applies to feet-anchored presets only (Waist and Custom with Attach to Camera off). Face and camera-attached presets always stay square to your view.
Heading
Applies to the feet-anchored Waist and Custom presets. Player Body keeps it at body heading, so turning your head does not move it. Camera Yaw turns it with your horizontal view.
Show Purple Fill
Draws the purple fill inside the purple panel. Turn it off to see only the white border ring.
Show Panel Border
Draws the white border ring around the purple panel. Turn it off to see only the HUD picture.
Hide Edge Lines
Stops thin purple lines showing at the edge of the white border ring, by running the purple fill under the ring.
Occlusion by Blocks & Entities

On: blocks and mobs between you and the purple panel hide it. Off: the panel draws over the world, and water and other translucent surfaces show through it. If that cannot start on your setup, the panel draws with occlusion on and the log says why.
Body Exclusion (First and Third Person)

In first and third person, the purple panel ignores blocks, mobs, your own body, hand, armour and particles, so it stays visible. Only applies when occlusion is on. Turn off to let blocks and mobs hide the panel where they cover it.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.panelW: Lets the purple panel lag behind your movement and catch up, instead of snapping. Choose which parts move with a lag below.
How long the heading and height take to catch up, in seconds. About 0.2 is a quick catch-up; larger values lag more.
How long the position takes to catch up, in seconds. Set separately, so position can lag more or less than the heading and height.
Lag the panel's turn and tilt, so it swings behind your view when you turn or look up and down.
Lag the panel's position, so it trails behind when you walk or sprint.
Lag the panel's height above your feet.
How much of the turn lag is shown, from 0 (locked to your body) to 100 (full lag). Scales the lag; it never overshoots.
How much of the position lag is shown, from 0 (no trailing) to 100 (full lag). Use this to calm the panel without changing its catch-up time.
The furthest the position lag may pull the panel away from its true place, in blocks. Caps how far it can trail when you sprint.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showSl: Include Hotbar Slot Cycling's side display (the cycle slots beside the hotbar) in the purple panel. The panel widens to hold it, so the hotbar appears slightly smaller. Turn off to keep the narrower picture.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.horizo: Picture Offset (%)
Moves the HUD picture inside the purple panel, in percent of the panel's height. Negative and positive values move it in opposite directions. The default is -4. -3 was the position confirmed in game.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.slotCy: How far the purple panel reaches from the centre of the hotbar, in GUI pixels, when Hotbar Slot Cycling Display is on. The default, 172, holds every cycle slot. Lower it to make the panel narrower, which cuts off the outer cycle slots. Has no effect when that display is off.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.horizo: Panel Preset

Chooses where the purple panel sits. Waist: anchored to your feet, using Panel Distance and Panel Height Above Feet. Face: fixed in your view, square to you, so it keeps its place on screen as you look around. The wiggle still lags its movement. Custom 1 and Custom 2: your own distance, height and anchor, set below.
Face: Distance
Face preset only. How far in front of the camera the purple panel sits, in blocks. The panel stays square to your view at this distance.
Face: Height vs Camera
Face preset only. Height of the panel above the centre of your view, in blocks. Negative puts it below the centre.
Custom 1: Distance
Custom 1 preset only. How far in front of its anchor the panel sits, in blocks.
Custom 1: Height
Custom 1 preset only. Height relative to its anchor, in blocks. With a feet anchor this is above your feet. With Attach to Camera on, it is above the centre of your view, and negative is below.
Custom 1: Attach to Camera
Custom 1 preset only. On: the panel stays fixed in your view, square to you, like Face. Off: it hangs from your feet, like Waist.
Custom 2: Distance
Custom 2 preset only. How far in front of its anchor the panel sits, in blocks.
Custom 2: Height
Custom 2 preset only. Height relative to its anchor, in blocks. With a feet anchor this is above your feet. With Attach to Camera on, it is above the centre of your view, and negative is below.
Custom 2: Attach to Camera
Custom 2 preset only. On: the panel stays fixed in your view, square to you, like Face. Off: it hangs from your feet, like Waist.
Move Panel for Shoulder Camera

For over-the-shoulder camera mods. When the camera sits beside you, the feet-anchored panel moves sideways by the same amount, so your body does not block it. Has no effect in first person, or on the Face and camera-attached presets.
